reachability.model: Finite least fixed point of script graph node plus correlated stage semantic state; every source choice is a structural candidate.
reachability.conditionalFeasibility: Story predicates, first-eligible hidden-choice precedence, and representative-witness evaluations are retained separately. Structural coverage does not assert that every branch is attainable in one story state.
reachability.routeWitnesses: Each semantic state has a deterministic breadth-first predecessor witness. Every tuple has a concrete first occurrence witness; visible tuples also have a first renderable witness.
reachability.timing: Operations apply in native timestamp/source order. Same-time operation intermediates are recorded as unpublished source states. Start/departure batches and local opacity intervals publish only where dialogue or a pending source cue leaves an observable interval.
reachability.counting: Playable source expressions are unique declared source-row IDs with a ready composition in a published visible interval. Literal NPC Expression 0 has no source animation row and remains explicit without counting as an authored expression. Source IDs, composition tuples, static portraits, hidden tuples and projected Rover expression IDs are counted separately.
reachability.coverageValidation: For every script, the correlated-state closure must cover exactly the independently traversed structural reachable nodes and choice edges.

limitations: Route enumeration abstracts external playthrough state and crosses conditional branches as explicit structural candidates; no global condition satisfiability claim is made.
Equivalent character membership/expression/visibility states share one representative source-position and source-entry witness. Their infinitely many loop histories are not duplicated.

Timed samples use locally settled phase-entry opacity. Cross-visit fade continuation, arbitrary player interruption times, CG occlusion and viewport cropping are retained as source metadata rather than certified framebuffer visibility.
Asset readiness here verifies registered resources and native clip existence. It does not itself observe browser rendering or native game playback.
Static source images have no authored Spine catchlight timeline. Text-only, missing-resource and unbound identities remain explicit inventory records.

occurrenceSchema.format: Dense rows use zero-based array indexes; row index is the row identity. Tuples and source operations are readable records.
sampleNames: after-source-operation; same-time batches may not publish this state
occurrenceSchema.join: observations[tupleIndex] → tuples[index]; observations[characterFrameId] → characterFrames[index]; characterFrames[contextId] → occurrenceContexts[index]; occurrenceContexts[stateIndex] → states[index]
occurrenceSchema.stateJoin: states.beforeStart and afterStart reference semanticCharacters[index]; states.outgoingTransitions reference graphTransitions[index]
occurrenceSchema.semanticCharacters: Readable records {id, who, expression, present, hasEntered, hidePortrait, hideAvatar, effect}. Expression is the literal source ID. portraitVisible = present && !hidePortrait; avatarVisible = present && !hideAvatar.
occurrenceSchema.pathJoin: Follow witnesses.parentStateId and viaEdgeId through source graph edges. A departure witnessId matches graphTransitions transitionId; its source state witness plus selected edge preserves the actual correlated path.
occurrenceSchema.visibility: Presence/hide flags are frame bits. Current speaker, node kind, source phase/time and publication interval are on the occurrence context. Per-composition eligibility/opacity are on the observation. Visibility labels choose a primary reason; tuple sourceHidden/nonPresent/nonSpeaker counters preserve each independent condition even when several apply.
